## Overview Fix `/generative_scoring` prompt construction when `item_first=true` and `add_special_tokens=true`: a BOS-adding tokenizer produced `item + BOS + query` instead of `BOS + item + query`, changing the scored input. Apply automatic special tokens to the first component in prompt order. ## Claims - Item-first requests produce the same scores as query-first requests with the fields exchanged, including mixed text/token-ID inputs. - Query-first requests, `add_special_tokens=false`, and fully pretokenized inputs retain their behavior; caller-supplied special tokens are preserved. - Add 10 real-server regression/control cases in the existing scoring suite and document the text/token-ID contract. ## Validation Source-built head `7f44f1516755494f11e93336bc48cb58471e75e5`, tested October 26-27, 2026, with real OPT-125m and Qwen3-0.6B weights: | Platform | Before fix: 10 regression/control cases | With fix: complete 30-test scoring suite | | --- | --- | --- | | Ryzen 9 7900X CPU | **3 failed, 7 passed** | **30 passed, 0 skipped** | | Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, ROCm / WSL2 | **3 failed, 7 passed** | **30 passed, 0 skipped** | The before runs retained the new tests and replaced only `serving.py` with base `a7407ab44557802ca32a0ba2c2707362d7d21563`. Both platforms failed the same three cases (`text-True`, `token_query-True`, `token_item-True`); the fixed runs had zero failures or setup errors, with assertions and tolerances unchanged. From a configured checkout, with the platform setup below: ```bash # Reproducer: fails on the base implementation, passes with the fix. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring_e2e.py::TestGenerativeScoringSpecialTokens -q --timeout=300 # Full scoring suite with the fix. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring -q --timeout=300 ``` Earlier macOS CPU inference validation compared three OPT-125m document/question pairs with independent Transformers inference: maximum score difference after the fix was `9.54e-7`. This checks inference consistency, not ranking quality or performance. **Coverage:** local V1-runner execution. Radeon required a local ROCm WSL GPU-selection backport and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.5`, described below. NVIDIA, multi-GPU and V2 execution were not run. The existing `entrypoints-integration-api-server-generate` Buildkite step selects this regression file; these local results do not establish upstream CI status.
CPU/Radeon environment and captured results - Ubuntu 22.04.5 under Windows 11 / WSL2; Python 3.12.14. Both checkouts were source-built at the head above. - Eager execution, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, cached weights with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. - `facebook/opt-125m`: float32, revision `27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`. - `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: bfloat16, revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. - CPU: PyTorch `2.14.0+cpu`, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1`, `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-11`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=12`; tcmalloc and libiomp5 preloaded. - Radeon: PyTorch `2.14.0+rocm10.1.0`, ROCm SDK 10.1.0 / HIP 7.16.26385, Windows driver `32.0.31041.5005`, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm`, `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1100`. - A local launcher added `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.5` to the real `vllm serve` command in both Radeon arms to leave VRAM for the Windows desktop. - The WSL runtime used a local backport of [ROCm/rocm-systems#14165](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/14165) onto ROCm 10.1 source `7da43026e4f2ef7600433c38c820732f7a205d22`. `LD_PRELOAD` selected the patched `librocdxg.so.1`, with `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` and `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`. This avoids a GPU-selection hang on a system with integrated and discrete AMD graphics; the workaround is outside this PR. Native HIP and float32/bfloat16 PyTorch matrix checks passed before the vLLM runs. The captured commands also used `--tb=short --junitxml=`. Pytest output: ```text CPU, before: 3 failed, 7 passed in 42.81s CPU, with fix: 30 passed in 66.44s Radeon, before: 3 failed, 7 passed, 1 warning in 67.70s Radeon, with fix: 30 passed, 1 warning in 135.52s ``` JUnit reports confirm zero setup errors and skips in all four completed runs. The warning was an optional TVM torch-C-DLPack allocator extension; model execution completed. These durations are test output, not a CPU/GPU benchmark. Production source was restored after the before runs.
Earlier macOS validation, model comparison, and lint macOS ARM64 CPU, Python 3.12, eager execution and V1 runner; OPT-125m float32 and Qwen3-0.6B bfloat16. On the earlier base `6f514338`, the new cases gave **3 failed, 7 passed**; with the fix, **10 passed**. The complete suite gave **30 passed**, using `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1`. The independent HTTP comparison used OPT-125m revision `27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`, three document/question pairs and the ` Yes`/` No` labels. The question was "Is this city the capital of France?" | Document | Before | With fix | Transformers on normally tokenized full text | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Paris | 0.70228010 | 0.57024276 | 0.57024181 | | London | 0.68276670 | 0.58552499 | 0.58552569 | | Berlin | 0.70646301 | 0.63823059 | 0.63823038 | All three corrected token sequences and scores matched the pretokenized reference exactly in that run. All 21 control prompt sequences were unchanged, including explicit token-ID inputs containing an internal special token. Maximum score difference from Transformers was `9.54e-7`. Applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint and CI test tethering; `git diff --check` passed: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/serving.py tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring_e2e.py docs/serving/online_serving/generative_scoring.md git diff --check ``` The hosted documentation preview has not been validated.
## Details `_build_prompts` always enabled automatic special tokens on the query and disabled them on each item, then concatenated according to `item_first`. The fix makes those two tokenization flags follow the requested order. Text components remain separately tokenized. A leading token-ID component is used as supplied, and its trailing text receives no automatic special tokens. The regression uses the existing query-first path with exchanged fields as its reference, through the real HTTP endpoint and model. It covers text/text, mixed text/token IDs, both special-token settings, and query-first controls. The serving guide and request-field documentation describe the same contract. **Related work / duplicate check:** #34539 introduced the endpoint. Refreshed open-PR searches for `generative_scoring`, `generative scoring` and `item_first` found no competing Python token-order fix, and current `main` still has the old construction. #46427 adds the separate Rust route; #61363 fixes renderer truncation. Neither fixes this Python prompt-construction path. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, validation and this description. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

files.patch:
@@ -18,6 +18,26 @@ This endpoint is automatically available when the server is started with a gener
 4. **Softmax Normalization**: Applies softmax over only the label tokens (when `apply_softmax=true`)
 5. **Score**: Returns the normalized probability of the first label token
 
+### Tokenization and special tokens
+
+Query and item strings are tokenized separately. With `add_special_tokens=true`
+(the default), the tokenizer adds its special tokens only to the first component
+in prompt order: the query by default (`item_first=false`), or the item when
+`item_first=true`.
+
+For a tokenizer that prepends a beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, text inputs
+produce:
+
+```text
+item_first=false: BOS + query tokens + item tokens
+item_first=true:  BOS + item tokens + query tokens
+```
+
+Token-ID inputs are used as provided, including any special tokens. If the first
+component is supplied as token IDs, no special tokens are automatically added to
+the following text component. Set `add_special_tokens=false` to disable automatic
+special tokens for all text inputs.
+
 ## Finding Token IDs
 
 To find the token IDs for your labels, use the tokenizer:

@@ -9,22 +9,27 @@
 import requests
 
 from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
 
 MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
+BOS_MODEL_NAME = "facebook/opt-125m"
 
 
 @pytest.fixture(scope="module")
-def server():
+def server(request):
+    model_name = getattr(request, "param", MODEL_NAME)
     args = [
         "--dtype",
-        "bfloat16",
+        "float32" if model_name == BOS_MODEL_NAME else "bfloat16",
         "--max-model-len",
         "512",
         "--enforce-eager",
         "--max-num-seqs",
-        "32",
+        "1" if model_name == BOS_MODEL_NAME else "32",
     ]
-    with RemoteOpenAIServer(MODEL_NAME, args) as remote_server:
+    if model_name == BOS_MODEL_NAME:
+        args += ["--no-enable-prefix-caching", "--kv-cache-memory-bytes", "268435456"]
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(model_name, args) as remote_server:
         yield remote_server
 
 
@@ -153,5 +158,76 @@ async def test_score_consistency(self, server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
         assert abs(r1_score - r2_score) < 1e-6
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("server", [BOS_MODEL_NAME], indirect=True)
+class TestGenerativeScoringSpecialTokens:
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("add_special_tokens", [False, True])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "query_as_tokens,item_as_tokens",
+        [(False, False), (True, False), (False, True), (True, True)],
+        ids=["text", "token_query", "token_item", "tokens"],
+    )
+    def test_item_first_matches_swapped_inputs(
+        self, server, add_special_tokens, query_as_tokens, item_as_tokens
+    ):
+        """Changing field order must not move or discard automatic special tokens."""
+        tokenizer = get_tokenizer(BOS_MODEL_NAME)
+        query = "\nQuestion: Is this city the capital of France?\nAnswer:"
+        item = "Document: Paris is the capital of France."
+        if query_as_tokens:
+            query = tokenizer.encode(query, add_special_tokens=True)
+        if item_as_tokens:
+            item = tokenizer.encode(item, add_special_tokens=True)
+        common = {
+            "model": BOS_MODEL_NAME,
+            "label_token_ids": [
+                tokenizer.encode(label, add_special_tokens=False)[0]
+                for label in (" Yes", " No")
+            ],
+            "add_special_tokens": add_special_tokens,
+        }
+        responses = [
+            requests.post(server.url_for("generative_scoring"), json=common | fields)
+            for fields in (
+                {"query": query, "items": [item], "item_first": True},
+                {"query": item, "items": [query], "item_first": False},
+            )
+        ]
+        for response in responses:
+            assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+        actual, reference = [response.json() for response in responses]
+        assert actual["usage"] == reference["usage"]
+        assert actual["data"][0]["score"] == pytest.approx(
+            reference["data"][0]["score"], abs=1e-6
+        )
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("add_special_tokens", [False, True])
+    def test_query_first_matches_pretokenized_prompt(self, server, add_special_tokens):
+        """Keep query-first tokenization and explicit token IDs unchanged."""
+        tokenizer = get_tokenizer(BOS_MODEL_NAME)
+        query = "Question: Is Paris the capital of France?"
+        item = "\nAnswer:"
+        prompt_ids = tokenizer.encode(query, add_special_tokens=add_special_tokens)
+        prompt_ids += tokenizer.encode(item, add_special_tokens=False)
+        common = {
+            "model": BOS_MODEL_NAME,
+            "label_token_ids": [3216, 440],  # OPT's " Yes" and " No" tokens.
+            "add_special_tokens": add_special_tokens,
+        }
+        responses = [
+            requests.post(server.url_for("generative_scoring"), json=common | fields)
+            for fields in (
+                {"query": query, "items": [item]},
+                {"query": prompt_ids, "items": [[]]},
+            )
+        ]
+        for response in responses:
+            assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+        actual, reference = [response.json() for response in responses]
+        assert actual["usage"] == reference["usage"]
+        assert actual["data"][0]["score"] == pytest.approx(
+            reference["data"][0]["score"], abs=1e-6
+        )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     pytest.main([__file__, "-v"])

@@ -54,7 +54,8 @@ class GenerativeScoringRequest(OpenAIBaseModel):
             the label_token_ids (True) or return true model probabilities over
             the full vocab for those ids (False).
         item_first: If True, prepend items to query. Otherwise append items to query.
-        add_special_tokens: Whether to add special tokens when tokenizing.
+        add_special_tokens: Whether to add special tokens when tokenizing the
+            first component of each prompt. Token-ID inputs are used as provided.
         cache_salt: Optional salt for prefix caching.
 
     """
@@ -86,7 +87,10 @@ class GenerativeScoringRequest(OpenAIBaseModel):
     )
     add_special_tokens: bool = Field(
         default=True,
-        description="Whether to add special tokens when tokenizing.",
+        description=(
+            "Whether to add special tokens when tokenizing the first component "
+            "of each prompt. Token-ID inputs are used as provided."
+        ),
     )
     cache_salt: str | None = Field(
         default=None,
@@ -378,11 +382,12 @@ async def _build_prompts(
             Tuple of (list of EngineInput, list of prompt token counts).
 
         """
-        # Tokenize query if it's a string
+        # Only the first component receives tokenizer-added special tokens.
         if isinstance(request.query, str):
             query_token_ids = tokenizer.encode(
                 request.query,
-                add_special_tokens=request.add_special_tokens,
+                add_special_tokens=request.add_special_tokens
+                and not request.item_first,
             )
         else:
             query_token_ids = request.query
@@ -393,10 +398,10 @@ async def _build_prompts(
         for item in request.items:
             # Tokenize item if it's a string
             if isinstance(item, str):
-                # Don't add special tokens for items to avoid duplicate BOS/EOS
                 item_token_ids = tokenizer.encode(
                     item,
-                    add_special_tokens=False,
+                    add_special_tokens=request.add_special_tokens
+                    and request.item_first,
                 )
             else:
                 item_token_ids = item
